evidence: the-monitoring-server-answers (nginx_frontend.pp:254-260): the location nginx_status (location /nginx_status, stub_status true, server $fqdn_monitoring_server, allow 127.0.0.1) supports the probe's request from 127.0.0.1 to http://<host>.monitoring.p8test.example.com/nginx_status, which expects 'Active connections: N'. The deny-all half of these lines is not probed (see purpose).

the-nginx-status-check-reports (nginx_frontend.pp:270-276): the file is root:root 0755 from check_nginx_status.py.erb. That template reads http://<fqdn_monitoring_server>/nginx_status and has defaults warn 50 / crit 100. -m sets the active-connections warning and -M the critical. The comparison is int(threshold) < value, and the active count is at least 1 (the check's own request), so 0 / 1 (WARNING) / 2 (CRITICAL) is what the code produces.

the-monitoring-server-answers (nginx_frontend.pp:222): $fqdn_monitoring_server = <trusted hostname>.monitoring.<domain>. With domain p8test.example.com and the node's short hostname, the name is $(hostname -s).monitoring.p8test.example.com. Line 265 pins it to 127.0.0.1 in /etc/hosts (getent), and lines 241-248 give return 200 'Hello World!\n' with default_type text/plain, matching the expected body and content type.

purpose gap: Tested on the applied node (my run ALL_PASS, every negative control failed on the clean node): HTTP to HTTPS 301 redirects for the domain and www, keeping path and query (nginx_frontend_domain.pp:420, 453); the HTTPS proxy to the backend under both names, with the certificate verified against the bundle's issuer and a mismatching name refused (521-524, 564); TLS 1.3 only (nginx_frontend.pp:42, 117-119); the default server's 404 over HTTP and HTTPS, with a mismatch control; the monitoring server pinned in /etc/hosts answering Hello World as text/plain; the Nagios check's OK, WARNING and CRITICAL exits. The uncovered rows are honest: fixture variants (ubuntu) and the RedHat key path (rhel9). GAP: lines 252-260 make the status page 'only accessible from localhost' (location_deny all, allow 127.0.0.1). The outcomes table does not list this restriction or mark it uncovered, and no check tests it, although the cited check derives from those very lines. The lab CAN test it on the node alone: my read-only request from the node to its own non-loopback addresses (--resolve <host>.monitoring.p8test.example.com:80:192.168.56.20 and :10.0.2.15) got 403, and the request from 127.0.0.1 got 200.
